lines.text: Swap one rotten plank on this ship. Is it still the same ship?
Swap another. And another. Until not one original piece is left.
Is it still the same thing?
For centuries, Athens kept the ship of Theseus, replacing every plank that rotted.
Plutarch says philosophers were already arguing about it.
In sixteen fifty-five, Thomas Hobbes made it worse.
What if you kept every old plank, and built them back together?
Now there are two ships. One without a single splinter of the original. One that is the original, whole.
So which one is the ship of Theseus?
Your body replaces about three hundred thirty billion cells a day. In three months, as many as you have in total.
Almost every cell in you is younger than you. Almost. The neurons in your cortex have been there since birth.
The trap was never the ship. It was the word, same.
Your matter changes every day, and no one doubts it's you.
